questions.q: Choose the correct verb: My cousin ___ a letter to me every month.
questions.explanation: A repeated action with a singular subject takes the simple present with -s.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: By the time the bell rang, the students ___ the paper.
questions.explanation: An action completed before a past event takes the past perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Neither of the two bags ___ mine, so please check again.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' with two singular items is treated as singular in standard exam usage: is.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The boys and the girls ___ practising for the annual day.
questions.explanation: A compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: Delhi is ___ capital of India.
questions.explanation: A unique, specific thing takes the definite article.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: There are ___ oranges in the basket, so we can make juice for everyone.
questions.explanation: 'Oranges' is countable and plural; 'a lot of' fits, while much, little and a little are used with uncountable nouns.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The tourists travelled ___ train from Pune to Nagpur.
questions.explanation: Means of transport takes 'by'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She will not attend the party ___ she is invited personally.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and gives the needed condition.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: When I was a child, I ___ climb that tree easily.
questions.explanation: 'Could' shows ability in the past.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'The farmer sells vegetables in the market.'
options: Vegetables are sold by the farmer in the market.
Vegetables were sold by the farmer in the market.
Vegetables sold by the farmer in the market.
Vegetables is sold by the farmer in the market.
questions.explanation: Simple present active becomes is/are + past participle; 'vegetables' is plural.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Tara said, 'I am going to the library now.'
options: Tara said that she is going to the library now.
Tara said that she was going to the library then.
Tara said that I was going to the library then.
Tara said that she went to the library then.
questions.explanation: 'Am going' becomes 'was going', 'I' becomes 'she', and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.q: Which sentence is the correct 'too ... to' form of 'The tea is so hot that I cannot drink it'?
options: The tea is too hot for me to drink.
The tea is too hot to not drink.
The tea is too much hot to drink it.
The tea is hot too to drink.
questions.explanation: 'Too + adjective + for + person + to + verb' has the same negative meaning.

questions.q: Which version of this sentence is punctuated correctly: 'Ananya my best friend lives in Surat'?
options: Ananya my best friend, lives in Surat.
Ananya, my best friend, lives in Surat.
Ananya my best friend lives, in Surat.
Ananya, my best friend lives in Surat.
questions.explanation: Commas enclose the phrase 'my best friend', which adds extra information.

questions.q: Which word is the antonym of 'transparent'?
questions.explanation: 'Opaque' means not allowing light to pass through, the opposite of transparent.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to cry over spilt milk' mean?
options: to be sad about a loss that cannot be undone
questions.explanation: It means to regret something that has already happened and cannot be changed.

questions.q: Rewrite in the past perfect tense: 'The guests left before the chief guest arrived.'
questions.answer: The guests had left before the chief guest arrived.
keyPoints: had + past participle for the earlier action
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The coach said to the team, 'Do not give up now.'
questions.answer: The coach told the team not to give up then.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with 'not to'.

questions.q: Rewrite as a complex sentence using 'if': 'Work hard to succeed in life.'
questions.answer: If you work hard, you will succeed in life.
keyPoints: main clause states the result with will
questions.explanation: An imperative of advice can be rewritten as a condition and result.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The committee has selected three students for the quiz.'
questions.answer: Three students have been selected for the quiz by the committee.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'quiet' and 'quite', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise: The library is quiet. 'Quite' means fairly or completely: The film was quite long.
questions.explanation: The words look alike but are different parts of speech with different meanings.
